prompt: An edge-to-edge repeating material sample of the interior metal bulkhead wall of the Leviathian, a Victorian steampunk submarine, seen straight on for a side-view adventure game. Broad riveted iron plates, subdued warm olive-brown and taupe aged metal, with some clearly visible but localized reddish-brown rust patches, small corrosion speckles and short rusty streaks beneath a few rivets. Subtle worn metal highlights and fine dark panel seams. Industrial nautical construction, unmistakably metal rather than masonry. Keep broad quiet areas and restrained contrast so foreground furniture and characters remain readable. Continuous opaque wall fills the whole square, with matching opposite edges for repetition horizontally and vertically, even illumination and no vignette or artificial frame. No floor, pipes, doors, portholes, furniture, gears, text or symbols. The first reference is an unscaled crop of the existing background, guiding dominant warm colors and the flat perspective, while its surface is redesigned as metal. The second reference, Churchill, guides only fine pixel detail, deliberate pixel clusters, restrained shading and the dark single-pixel contour treatment; do not reproduce the character or clothing. The third reference, quill and inkwell, guides fine dark contours only. Apply that fine contour language to plate joints and rivets without thick black bars or an outer canvas border. The fourth reference is the game's color swatch sheet, guiding colors only, with additional harmonious metal and rust shades allowed. Sharp stepped pixel shapes, no blur or antialiasing.
